chapter: Chicago bands and the Charlie Cook circle
title: Margie Lewis and Charlie Cook's arrangements of classics
summary: His genius pianist Margie Lewis swung classics; Charlie Cook arranged small-band swing versions at the Lyon & Healy building.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And so at that time I'm on drums and I had a woman playing piano with me that her fingers were so extra long they were just about half again as long as mine. And she was one of Clarence Jones the scholars and she was a genius at the piano. And she could cover tense with just laying her hands on the piano with full harmony. I brought her from the west side over here to the south side and I organized this little band and the reason I mentioned her about her being a genius in which nobody on the south side knows she was a great classic and I schooled her in how to swing and jazz and I know that she could take classics and cut them up and improvise it in this jazz form. And my ideas of playing jazz all the time because I played around them white saloons in Louisville and I had to play the national hammering and everything in jazz temple to get my money. And so I was used to that. And so when I got this little band and brought them out there I used all that kind of stuff because the type of band that I had was men in a band that could play that stuff and improvise it. Now to help me to get this stuff arranged like that my cousin was a great artist in music and you might know of him Dr. Charlie Cook.
Oh yes. I met him years ago.

Well now when he had his ranging office down in Lyon Healy building I went down there and explained to him what I was in for and what I wanted to do. I said Margie Lewis is a great pianist. I said you have never seen her. I said but I know that she can cut it. I said she can hold so much harmony on the piano and I got a trombone player from Louisville that used to play violin and could play trumpet and he could take trombone and play off a violin sheet and play the leads and he could sing tenor and so we're all doubling like that and the trumpet player could double on violin which was Ray Mack I said I want you to arrange me a nice little arrangement and a melody in F in the jazz form see and he said what do you want to take a number like that buddy and cut it up like I said will you arrange this with a small arrangement and fill it full harmony so that I can produce this thing out there I said something new he said well I laughed like if you want it that way I'm going to fix that way and I'm coming out and listen to see what it sounds like that is the first beginning of that type of a musician taking classics and arranging them into swing form Charlie Cook could you
